subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service disable for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override stale generated service-env, state-dir `.env`, and config env values on macOS LaunchAgent gateways?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain private prompts and tool output, so automation should not choose whether an explicit false/unset launchd signal or durable service configuration is the authoritative operator intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat unset, `0`, `off`, and `false` as authoritative disable intent for managed services, clear or override stale generated raw-stream service-env entries, and document that precedence.

options.title: Durable Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config env authoritative, and document that operators must remove those durable values before restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor-Guided Repair
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add doctor/status detection and repair for stale raw-stream service env before operators believe logging is off.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat unset, `0`, `off`, and `false` as authoritative disable intent for managed services, clear or override stale generated raw-stream service-env entries, and document that precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the raw-stream flag surface and has the strongest adjacent history across the daemon/LaunchAgent lifecycle code.
